subject.title: fix(plugins): run message_sending on all channel agent-reply deliveries (#92374)

question: Should Telegram own `message_sending` at delivery time through the internal `runsMessageSendingAtDelivery` opt-out, or should the shared dispatcher remain the single pre-delivery safety-hook owner?
rationale: Both choices can fix the bypass, but they define the permanent safety-hook boundary for channel delivery and exactly-once semantics; that is maintainer intent, not a mechanical review choice.

options.title: Allow Telegram-owned delivery gate after repair
options.body: Keep the opt-out approach, fix suffix no-reentry, and require current-head proof that `message_sending` runs exactly once for normal, streamed, rewritten, cancelled, and long-suffix replies.

options.title: Move the gate back to the dispatcher
options.body: Remove the opt-out and rework Telegram streaming so the shared dispatcher owns the hook without per-block or duplicate invocation.

options.title: Split the fix scope
options.body: Land a narrower configured-dispatcher repair first and keep Telegram streamed-final gating tracked on the canonical issue until the ownership boundary is settled.

recommendation.title: Allow Telegram-owned delivery gate after repair
recommendation.body: Keep the opt-out approach, fix suffix no-reentry, and require current-head proof that `message_sending` runs exactly once for normal, streamed, rewritten, cancelled, and long-suffix replies.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision turns on the plugin hook contract and dispatcher composition area introduced in `b474f429ee4b`, with Telegram owners as follow-up reviewers.
